items.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Now you played some behind Ella Fitzgerald. ... you’re playing for her

ctx.x: Now you played some behind Ella Fitzgerald. How is it different to accompany a singer, especially a great singer?

Oh and she is the greatest. Ella, for instance when she was singing the verse to a tune, out of time you know, and you’re playing for her, you just kind of have to tag after her. Because she goes right through it — bang you know. Now somebody like, oh I can’t © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

think of the names but it doesn’t matter, maybe I’ll think of it later, sing way behind the beat. I mean way behind the beat. You’ve got to be tugging them, like with a rope you know. Not that it’s bad, it’s just that you have to learn how to do with each singer.

items.title: Herb Ellis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: What made Ella Fitzgerald such a great singer in your mind? ... She just had all the qualities. ... Probably the world’s greatest singer to date.

ctx.x: That’s wild. What made Ella Fitzgerald such a great singer in your mind?
She just had all the qualities. She had a melodic content, the sound, the phrasing. Everything. Probably the world’s greatest singer to date.
